findings.claim: The helper can apply a non-idempotent operation more than once when the operation succeeds remotely or mutates state and then raises an ambiguous transient error.
evidence: src/retry.py:7-11 reruns the same arbitrary callable after every caught Exception and provides no idempotency key, deduplication, or restriction to side-effect-free operations.
A focused runtime check used an operation that appended one write and then raised TimeoutError on its first call; call_with_retry returned successfully after the second call with two writes recorded.

findings.claim: All ordinary exceptions are treated as retryable, so deterministic application and validation failures are repeated instead of failing immediately.
evidence: src/retry.py:10 catches Exception without classifying transient versus permanent failures.
A focused runtime check with an operation that always raised ValueError('invalid request') showed that the operation was invoked three times before the ValueError was returned to the caller.
tests/test_retry.py:4-15 covers only recovery from TimeoutError and does not constrain which exception types may be retried.

findings.claim: Retries have no delay, exponential backoff, jitter, or server-directed pacing, allowing many callers to hammer a degraded dependency in tight synchronized loops and worsen an outage.
evidence: src/retry.py:7-11 immediately begins the next loop iteration after an exception; there is no sleep or backoff calculation.
A focused runtime check completed 1,000 failing attempts in approximately 0.000354 seconds, confirming that retries are issued as a tight loop.

findings.claim: Non-positive attempt counts do not produce a defined validation error and instead fail through an internal assertion before the operation is called.
evidence: src/retry.py:7 executes zero iterations for attempts <= 0, leaving last_error as None; src/retry.py:13 then raises AssertionError.
Focused runtime checks with attempts=0 and attempts=-1 both raised an empty AssertionError and invoked the operation zero times.

Because Python assertions can be disabled with optimization, the same path can instead proceed to `raise None` and produce a different TypeError, making production behavior dependent on interpreter flags.

uncertainties: The case contains no call sites, so it is unknown whether production callers independently enforce idempotency, restrict retryable exception types, or cap the attempts argument.
The required retry timing and backoff policy is not specified; the finding is based on the observed absence of any pacing in this helper.
